text:
maya: Heads-up — nightly perf-run 03:00 showed a spike in OOMs on the gpus after the kernel-selector change landed. Not sure if it's kernel selection or a reuse/lease regression.
liam: saw the same. CI logs show a bunch of small allocations around logits buffers that never freed between micro-batches.
sarah: pinging the perf bot to attach the heap profile + alloc trace.
perf-bot: Attached: /artifacts/perf/2573456789/heap_profile.pb.gz, alloc-trace.txt (sampled).
maya: quick numbers from the run: peak_mem per-GPU went 9.8GB -> 12.4GB, alloc_count for logits_slab +30%, scratchpad_reclaims down 42%. KV cache hit rate unchanged ~85%.
liam: kernel-selector notes: we now prefer fused-attn kernel 'attn_fused_v2' for seq<=128. That changes workspace assumptions (smaller temp needed) but I wonder if runtime still preallocs older scratch sizes for backward compatibility.
sarah: I profiled allocation sites. Most extra allocations originate from logits_pack() path when streaming + batch_size==1. It creates a transient tensor, then we attempt to place it into the logits_slab with lease=inf instead of short-lived.
tony: reproduce locally with this command: 
```
PYTHONPATH=./python ./tools/run_infer.py --model redwood/small --seq 64 --streams 30 --batching micro
```
maya: when I repro'd, setting env OPT_SLAB_LEASE_MS=50 avoided the OOM. But that felt like papering over the root cause.
liam: agree — we should change the default for logits scratch leases in streaming mode to ephemeral. Proposed change: if request is streaming or batch_size==1, set slab_lease_policy=ephemeral; otherwise default=shared.
sarah: also propose an allocator tweak: mark logits buffers as "eager-free candidate" when they are produced after final-token logits and not referenced by KV cache. That lets the slab runtime attempt immediate reclamation between micro-batches.
maya: quick patch I put in a branch, here's the core of the change: 
```
# runtime/scratch/slab_manager.py
if is_streaming or batch_size == 1:
    slab.alloc_flags |= ALLOC_EPHEMERAL
else:
    slab.alloc_flags &= ~ALLOC_EPHEMERAL

# when tensor refcount drops to 0:
if tensor.alloc_flags & ALLOC_EPHEMERAL:
    slab.eager_free(tensor)
```

liam: nice. any perf regressions from that?
maya: ran unit microbenchmarks — token throughput unchanged for standard batches, latency for micro-batches improved ~6% p50, memory peak lowered ~1.8GB on the test rig. But on the nightly large-regression run, kernel-selector combos still produced 1 OOM in 10 runs.
sarah: we might be hitting a race: kernel_selector decides fused kernel requiring smaller workspace, but the older allocation path preallocs both fused and unfused workspace for safety. If ephemeral frees happen but the prealloc slab still has reserved chunks, the runtime tries to hand out a chunk that overlaps with pinned logits memory.
tony: can we change preallocation to lazy-reserve: reserve metadata only, not physical GPU memory until first use? That would reduce pinned footprint. Might require more bookkeeping but seems the right long-term fix.
liam: agreed, but that is bigger. Short-term mitigation: 1) short slab leases for logits in streaming mode, 2) eager-free for ephemeral tensors, 3) adjust kernel-selector to avoid fused/unfused mixed prealloc in the same instance (prefer consistent kernel family per-serving-worker).
maya: +1. I'd like an experiment plan: can someone run 5k streaming requests on canary with the two short-term changes and report OOM rate and peak mem distribution?
sarah: I'll run it today on canary pool c-asia-2. Plan: baseline (current main), patch1 (slab_lease_ephemeral), patch2 (ephemeral eager-free), patch3 (both). Metrics: peak_mem, alloc_count, slab_reclaims, OOMs, p50/p95 latency.
ton y: (typo) tony: I'll tweak the kernel-selector canary to bias towards non-fused for seq<=64 for a set of 10 workers so we can test 'consistent kernel family' hypothesis.
liam: add a profiler marker for "slab_eager_free" and "slab_lease_expired" so we can count events. Put them into tracing so console can plot over time.
maya: one more idea — KV cache behavior: when we mark logits ephemeral, ensure we don't evict a KV page that will be needed immediately; add a grace window (2 requests) before eviction for pages recently touched by streaming sessions. That should smooth churn.
sarah: noted. I'll gate that behind a flag `kv.eviction_grace_ms` and start with 200ms.
maya: ok let's coordinate: Sarah runs the canary + perf collection; Tony toggles kernel bias; Liam adds trace markers; I'll own the slab lease default change PR. Can we aim to have results by EOD tomorrow?
liam: should be doable. I'll open the trace PR now.
sarah: starting baseline run now. uploading logs to /artifacts/perf/2573456789/baseline/
perf-bot: Run started: run-id=perf-2573456789-1. ETA ~2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya: thanks all. If we see OOMs persist after short-term mitigations, we'll revert the kernel-selector change until lazy-reserve is implemented.
liam: note for the rollback: ensure model pinning unaffected — add a post-deploy job to validate kernel family consistency per-worker.
tony: thanks. tagging @infra on the canary pool knobs in case we need capacity changes. :thumbsup:
maya: I'll update the rollout checklist in the PR with the canary links and metrics to watch.
